correctness.rationale: With coefficient mask m=sum c_ij 2^(4j+i), exactly three rational linear cubes give total fibres. The 65535 masks exhaust H0(O(3,3)) minus zero. A direct obstruction finds 1128 candidates for >3 totals, of which 1110 have rational singularities; the residual 18 form a single 72-group orbit singular over F4 at (alpha,alpha+1) for mask 6854. The full census has 49515 explicitly verified singular witnesses, 16020 survivors partitioned into 252 orbits, and 1008 Groebner unit ideals on all four affine charts of their representatives. Independent direct and orbit-weighted six-bin counts agree. The equal-zeta pair masks 6335/10685 is smooth with N1..N4=(2,8,17,20). Executable files code/count_singular.cpp, code/verify_negative.py, code/group_orbits.py, code/branch_census.py, code/verify_positive.py, code/verify_sharp_bound.py and code/verify_zeta_collision.py reproduce these facts. The bounded field search is used only for negative witnesses, never as a positive smoothness proof.

value.rationale: Each canonical split-quadric genus-four curve has two naturally defined trigonal maps; comparing their rational total ramification is an intrinsic geometric question connected to degree-12 branch discriminants. The sharp bound t1+t2<=3 is stronger than the trivial individual ceiling three and is proved by an independent sharp obstruction. The complete six-profile counts identify exact realizability and 252-isomorphism-class frequencies. Explicit equal-zeta smooth examples prove that paired total ramification contains arithmetic geometry beyond the prior point-count/Weil-census data. This is not merely a routine restatement of the underlying genus-four curve enumeration; no claim outside the stated finite-field family is made.
